title: VSift ingest data v1
description: The data member of a complete ingest result. transcript is present only when a supplied transcript was imported with the session; a plain ingest omits it. time_anchor is present only when the session has a clock-time anchor. origin is present only for a source fetched with ingest --url (0.3.0). publication is the session's own guarantee: process_crash_consistent, or os_crash_durable for a durable session on the qualified profile (P10 engine API; P11 durable workspaces). Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json.

time_anchor.description: When the recording happened by the real-world clock, and on what authority (time anchoring, 0.3.0): from ingest --recorded-at, else the container's recording-time tags, which a plain ingest reads with one FFprobe run when the media tools are set up and verified. Absent when no clock time is known.

origin.description: Where a source fetched with ingest --url came from (0.3.0, ADR 0028); absent for a local file's copy: direct_origin for a direct link, page_origin for a public video page fetched through yt-dlp.

page_origin.description: A public page fetched through yt-dlp. It never holds the link, a title, an uploader, a description, an upload date, a format's URL or a header. provider is yt-dlp's name for the site. video_id is present only when the site reports the video public; otherwise video_id_sha256 holds the id's digest, because an unlisted video's id is a capability token. yt_dlp and js_runtime say which tools ran: source managed with catalogue_version, or user_managed with the version line and SHA-256 of a file nobody here reviewed; js_runtime is absent when none ran. address_check is proxy_resolved when a proxy from the environment made yt-dlp's connections, and absent otherwise: VSift checks no address yt-dlp connects to. joined says whether the source was one file or separate audio and video joined by a stream copy.

direct_origin.description: A direct link. It never holds the link, which may carry a signed token in its query or its path: link_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the link as given after parsing (query included), so the same link can be recognised but not recovered. requested_host is the link's host and final_host the host the bytes came from after redirects (at most three). address_check is direct when VSift resolved the name and connected only to public addresses it checked, and proxy_resolved when a proxy from the environment resolved it (VSift then refused only internal-looking names and addresses). retrieved_at is when the body was complete; bytes is the source's size. A provider's upload date is not a recording time and is never recorded.
